served: needle EMG of the affected muscles
results: 1. anti-aquaporin-4 and anti-MOG antibodies: BOTH NEGATIVE - not neuromyelitis optica or MOG-antibody disease
2. cervical and whole spine MRI: LONGITUDINALLY EXTENSIVE T2 lesion confined to the cervical cord
3. needle EMG of the affected muscles: prolonged bursts, overflow activation and simultaneous agonist-antagonist contraction, with NO denervation or myopathy - confirms dystonic hypertonia
4. corticosteroid trial: high-dose intravenous methylprednisolone 1 g/day for five days followed by an oral taper
dx_raw:
DIAGNOSIS: Seronegative autoimmune longitudinally extensive transverse myelitis confined to the cervical spinal cord, causing secondary spinal dystonia with dystonic hypertonia.

ALTERNATIVE 1: Stiff-person spectrum disorder with spinal-predominant dystonia.

ALTERNATIVE 2: Functional neurological movement disorder.

ALTERNATIVE 3: Structural cervical myelopathy causing secondary dystonia.
